source_review: Actual frame stores destroy target, backend handle, Busy/Closing gate and concrete closure environment. Allocation failure destroys the prepared environment once. Installation initializes all fields before a possible synchronous callback; null installation relies on the explicit backend no-future/all-accesses-ended promise, then destroys the environment and frees the frame once.

Atomic fetch-or Busy admits only old=0. Rejected old=Busy or Busy|Closing does not clear another invocation's Busy bit. Old=Closing temporarily acquired Busy and clears only that bit. Invocation exit preserves Closing. This gate establishes exclusive access to F, not raw-entry quiescence.

Close sets Closing before calling the actual supplied close target. The strong foreign contract must drain every raw entry/access, including entries before admission and rejected entries, and forbid future access before returning. Only then does the implementation assert gate=Closing, drop F and free. Default Drop uses the same close path; a null owner is a valid empty state.

Both kernels independently derive concrete F, canonical owning payload, exact external register/close role signatures, recursive closed capture graph and Direct code dependencies. ClosedEnvironment denies stored Address/Desc/Slice/unresolved positions. Code-pointer signature addresses are not confused with captured data addresses.

The generic factory exemption requires exactly one actual F input, finite Copy companions and Create/Give returned Registration of that same concrete environment. Closure captures are independently closed and ordinary ownership checks still enforce actual transfer and cleanup; no synchronous noescape trace grants retained borrowed-storage permission.

Previously identified metering seams are corrected: recursive finite-Copy and entry signature comparisons are prepaid independently; actual Register/Close symbol lengths are charged per generated site; physical inline layout walks pay repeated closure occurrences with an active-path cycle guard, stopping at dynamic owning heads instead of deduplicating all ClosureIds.

Current callback signature is Fn/FnMut(i32)->i32. General Task owned parameters/results, child frames, PendingExit and asynchronous waker drainage remain open.

Native executables are ephemeral test outputs; the retained Rust harness and runtime-read C inputs are bound, with actual native executions observed during this replay.
